source.author: verg
source.text: Non, mihi si linguae centum sint oraque centum, ferrea vox, omnis scelerum comprendere formas, omnia poenarum percurrere nomina possim.
source.text_original: Non, mihi si linguae centum sint oraque centum, / ferrea vox, omnis scelerum comprendere formas, / omnia poenarum percurrere nomina possim.'
source.text_english: No, even if I had a hundred tongues, a hundred mouths, and a voice of iron, I could not comprehend all the forms of crimes, nor run through all the names of punishments.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: alius tumenti aqualiculo mortem parturit; alius elinguis et mutus et ne hoc quidem habens, unde roget, magis rogat, quia rogare non potest; hic debilitatus a paruo non sibi mendicat stipem; ille putrefactus morbo regio superuiuit cadaueri suo: non, mihi si linguae centum sint oraque centum, omnia poenarum percurrere nomina possim.
reuse.text_original: alius tumenti aqualiculo mortem parturit; alius elinguis et mutus et ne hoc quidem habens, unde roget, magis rogat, quia rogare non potest; hic debilitatus a paruo non sibi mendicat stipem; ille putrefactus morbo regio superuiuit cadaueri suo: non, mihi si linguae centum sint oraque centum, omnia poenarum percurrere nomina possim.
reuse.text_english: One man, with his belly swollen, breeds death; another, speechless and mute, and not even having this, whereby he might ask, begs all the more because he cannot beg; this man, weakened to a little body, does not beg alms for himself; that one, rotted by jaundice, has outlived his own corpse. If I had a hundred tongues and a hundred mouths, I could not run through all the names of the punishments.
